item.description: Simon Stiell makes opening address at summit in Turkey, where talks are under way about speeding up shift to electrification A global fossil fuel price crisis is “spreading inflation like a cancer” around the planet, the UN’s chief climate negotiator, Simon Stiell, told the opening plenary of critical UN climate talks in Turkey. item.title: Smart use of trees and crops brings best yield
item.description: Cultivating crops—such as wheat, barley and rye—alongside rows of trees is a system of agroforestry that is known as "alley-cropping." It serves many functions: in addition to enhancing ecosystems and biodiversity, it can also counteract the negative effects of growing crops in treeless open land. The advantages of alley-cropping come from the interaction between trees and crops, resulting in improved soil quality, reduced wind erosion, enhanced nutrient cycling, and climate change mitigation through increased carbon capture. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Ecuador: ¿qué han cambiado 1.000 días de estado de excepción?
item.description: Ecuador cumple 1.000 días bajo estados de excepción desde enero de 2024, una estrategia que ha normalizado la presencia militar en las calles. Las cifras oficiales registraron menos homicidios en 2024, pero la violencia repuntó en 2025 hasta un récord histórico. En 2026, pese a un nuevo descenso, los asesinatos siguen superando los 20 diarios. Desde Guayaquil, analizamos qué ha cambiado en la seguridad del país, el impacto de la militarización y las consecuencias de prolongar las medidas extraordinarias durante casi tres años. Reportaje de Carolina Mella para France 24. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

El líder de la Iglesia católica está saldando una deuda que el Vaticano tenía pendiente desde el pontificado de Francisco, que no visitó su país natal en sus 12 años de pontificado. item.title: COP31 climate summit: Can we electrify the world?
item.description: The UN's annual climate change summit, known as COP31, opens this Monday in Turkey amid deep concern following deadly heatwaves in Europe and deadly floods in Nepal. A "super El Niño" in the Pacific is also expected to drive more extreme weather events. In response, COP31 host Turkey is set to launch a global initiative aiming to electrify a third of the world economy. FRANCE 24's Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe tells us more. Fuente: France 24 - English.
